title: How to Plan for Retirement When You Anticipate High Longevity
description: Funding a 40-year retirement if you expect to live to 100.
content:
Living to 100 is a blessing, but financially, it is a risk. 'Longevity Risk' is the danger of outliving your money. A plan designed to last to age 85 will fail catastrophically if you live to 102. If you have a family history of longevity or are in excellent health, you must structure your retirement differently. You need a higher equity allocation (to fight 40 years of inflation) and specific insurance products (like longevity annuities) to guarantee you don't die broke.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Inflation' Threat: Over 35-40 years, prices will triple. A safe 'Bond Heavy' portfolio will lose purchasing power. You must hold 50%+ Stocks even at age 80 to keep up.
  • Deferred Annuities (QLAC): A Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract allows you to buy a pension at age 65 that doesn't start paying until age 85. It is cheap 'Old Age Insurance'.
  • Social Security Optimization: Delaying to age 70 is non-negotiable. You need the maximum possible inflation-adjusted government check to cover your 90s.
  • Withdrawal Rate Adjustment: The 4% rule assumes 30 years. For 40 years, aim for 3.3% to 3.5%. This requires a larger nest egg.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The actuarial tables suggest a 65-year-old couple has a 50% chance of one spouse living to 92. Planning for age 95 or 100 is not optimistic; it is prudent risk management.

The Centenarian Portfolio

Standard advice says 'Age in Bonds'. For you, that is dangerous.

The Equity Glidepath

Standard Advice: At 80, hold 20% Stocks.
Longevity Advice: At 80, hold 50% Stocks.
Why? You might have 20 years left. You still need growth. Bonds paying 4% won't keep up with medical inflation of 6%.

The QLAC Strategy

You take $200,000 of your IRA at age 65. You buy a QLAC.
It pays $0 for 20 years.
At age 85, it starts paying $4,000/month for life.
Benefit: You now have permission to spend your other assets aggressively from 65-85, knowing the 'Old Age' check kicks in later.

Housing as the Reserve

Keep your home. If you run out of liquid cash at 95, a Reverse Mortgage can tap the home equity to pay for in-home care. It is the asset of last resort.

Health-Wealth Connection

  1. Healthspan vs Lifespan: Living to 100 in bad health is expensive (Nursing Home). Living to 100 in good health is cheaper (Travel/Food). Invest in fitness/diet as a financial strategy.
  2. Long-Term Care: You are almost guaranteed to need care if you live to 100. Self-insure with a $300k dedicated fund, or buy a Hybrid Life/LTC policy.
  3. Roth Conversions: Since you have a long timeline, the tax-free compounding of a Roth is more valuable. Convert aggressively in your 60s to let it grow for your 90s.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I die early?

Then you leave a massive inheritance. That is the 'Risk' of over-saving. Most people prefer leaving money to heirs over running out of money at 95.

Is a QLAC safe?

Yes, if bought from top-rated insurers. State Guaranty Associations also provide a layer of protection (limits apply). Diversify across carriers if buying large amounts.

Can I spend principal?

Yes. But calculate carefully. RMD tables are designed to drain your IRA by roughly age 120. Following the RMD withdrawal method prevents you from hitting $0.
